DILG BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http:\/ymnw.dilg_gov_ph S. 2014 OPINION NO Cl MAY22 KRISTINE S. CO Chief Compliance Officer PPC Asia Corporation 28th & 29th Floors, The Upper Class Tower, Quezon Avenue cor. Sct. Reyes St., Barangay Paligsahan, Quezon City Dear Ms. CO. This refers to your letter dated 23 February 2024 in relation to your company's personnel who are also incumbent barangay officials. Per your representation, one of your sales personnel in Tacloban City has been a barangay kagawad even before he joined your company in 2019. Subsequently, he sought re-election last 30 October 2023 Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE), and won for his second term as barangay kagawad, without informing your company. Similarly, another one of your sales personnel won as a barangay kagawad in the last BSKE, and likewise did not inform your company, before, during, and after the elections that he filed his candidacy, campaigned, and was elected as a barangay official. Under this premise arose your request for this Office to provide a clarification to protect both the rights and interests of the parties involved, including your company, particularly on the following: I. In view of Sec. 12, Rule XVIII of the Revised Civil Service Rules, is the written permission from the Office of the Secretary a requisite before they can engage in private employment? 2. Does the phrase "practice of profession" confined or limited to professions regulated by the Professional Regulations Commission (PRC) and the Supreme Court? 3. Do the sales personnel, who are also public officials, create undue pressure to companies in the area where the sales personnel operate, results in unfair competition among other players in the area? 4. Can this be a valid ground to impose administrative disciplinary action against these sales personnel? "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Trunkline: (02) 8876-3454

5. Does the concealment of these sales personnel as public official and running for public office constitute bad faith including the non-filing of application for leave of absence from the company whenever they attend or attended public functions and activities? 6. There is conflict of interest. Considering that the ISt and 2nd queries are interrelated, allow us to address them in one discussion. As to the first query, we answer in the negative. At the onset, we would like to highlight the pronouncement of the Supreme Court in the case of Catu v. Rellosal, that Section 90 of Republic Act 7160 of the Local Government Code is a special provision that applies specifically to the practice of profession by elective local officials. As a special law with a definite scope (that is, the practice of profession by elective local officials), it constitutes an exception to Section 7(b)(2) of RA 6713, the general law on engaging in the private practice of profession by public officials and employees. Section 90 of Republic Act No. 7160 otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" ("LGC"), which pertains to the practice of profession of elective local government officials, to wit: SECTION 90. Practice of Profession. — (a) All governors, city and municipal mayors are prohibited from practicing their profession or engaging in any occupation other than the exercise of their functions as local chief executives. (b) Sanggunian members may practice their professions, engage in any occupation, or teach in schools except during session hours: Provided, That sanggunian members who are also members of the Bar shall not: xxx As can be gleaned from the foregoing, governors, city and municipal mayors are prohibited from practicing their profession or engaging in other profession because they are required to render full service in serving the people. However, no such interdiction is made on the punong barangay and the members of the sangguniang barangay - Expressio unius est exclusio alterius. Since they are excluded from any prohibition, the presumption is that they are allowed to practice their profession. This stands to reason because they are not mandated to serve full time. In fact, the sangguniang barangay is supposed to hold regular sessions only twice a month. Correspondingly, this Department has been consistent with its opinion that elective barangay officials are allowed to engage in other occupation other than the exercise of their functions as Punong Barangays or as members of the sangguniang barangay. Note, however, that in case of a punong barangay and/or a member of the sangguniang barangay who intends to practice his/her profession, must first obtain prior written permission from the head of the Department concerned as required by civil service regulations. 1 A.C. No. 5738, February 19, 2008. Page 2 of 4

As to the 2nd query, we answer in the affirmative. Under Sec. 1 (b) of Resolution no. 2012-668, series of 2012, issued by the Professional Regulation Commission, "Practice of Profession" refers to an activity/undertaking rendered by a registered and licensed professional or a holder of a Special Temporary Permit as defined in the scope of practice of professional regulatory law. In Legal Opinion No. 5, series of 2019, this Department had the occasion to differentiate "practice of profession" and "engaged in any occupation". The Department had this to say: Xxx it bears to note that the Local Government Code of 1991 did not define the phrase "practice of profession" not did it define the phrase "engage in an occupation". Hence, the general rule in construing words and phrases used in law (in the) absence of a legislative intent to the contrary, it should be given their plain, ordinary, and common meaning. Hence, in the furtherance of this discussion, we deemed it proper to revisit the meaning of the words tangent to our elucidation, Webster Dictionary defines profession as a calling requiring specialized knowledge and often long and intensive academic preparation. On the other hand, occupation has been commonly defined as an activity in which one is engaged into. Hence, apparently, there is a distinction between the two in that, to exercise profession means that one has to be academically prepared. Take the government examination and pass it and is registered in a government licensing body which regulates such profession. On the other hand, when one's activity does not fall within the ambit of "exercise of profession", the same can properly fall under engage in any occupation. Therefore, the barangay officials working as sales personnel in your company, are not considered as "practicing a profession", but are only engaged in another occupation. Hence, prior written authorization from the Office of the Secretary is not a requisite, and they are allowed to engage in such occupation. In addition, while there is no query pertaining to issue of double compensation, we deem it proper to clarify that this Department has been consistent with its opinion that the prohibition on double compensation applies only to appointment to public office of position and not to a private office. Proceeding to your 4th query regarding possibility of filing an administrative disciplinary action and your 5th query, we would like to emphasize that the grounds set forth under Section 602 of the LGC pertains to acts in relation to their duty, or while acting in their official capacity as an elected public official or as barangay officials, and does not include private employment. 2 SECTION 60. Grounds for Disciplinary Actions. — An elective local official may be disciplined, suspended, Or removed from office on any Of the following grounds: (a) Disloyalty to the Republic Of the Philippines; (b) Culpable violation of the Constitution; (c) Dishonesty. oppression, misconduct in office, gross negligence, or dereliction of duty; (d) Commission of any offense involving moral turpitude or an offense punishable by at least prision mayor; (e) Abuse of authority: (f) Unauthorized absence for fifteen (15) consecutive working days, except in the case Of members of the sangguniang panlalawigan, sangguniang panlungsod, sangguniang bayan, and Sangguniang barangay; (g) Application for, or acquisition of, foreign citizenship or residence or the status of an immigrant of another country; and (h) Such other grounds as may be provided in this Code and other laws. An elective local official may be removed from office on the grounds enumerated above by order of the proper court. Page 3 Of 4

Similarly, in relation to your 3rd and 6th queries, conflict of interest arises whenever a public official or employee, by faithfully performing his official duty, may oppose or affect the interest of a private corporation or business to which he is also affiliated, either as member of a boards, officer or a substantial stockholder. In other words, if the faithful performance of his official duty will not oppose or affect the interest of a private corporation or business to which he is affiliated, there is no conflict of interest to speak of. Thus, conflict of interest does not ipso facto arise whenever a public official or employee holds another position in a private corporation or business. Notwithstanding the foregoing, as to the issues contained in queries 3-6, we are of the position that these circumstances are best to be evaluated by your company considering that it pertains to internal matters governed by the company's Code of Conduct or guidelines. This opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you Very truly yours, BY TH UTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: AN VICTOR R.
